steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: The interview is being held here? How unconventional.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: When you applied to be the MBCC Chief, did you have your interview here as well?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...The situation at the time was quite unique. I was directly appointed without an interview.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: How lucky. You avoided a lot of trouble, then.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If you were in my position, you wouldn't say that. Let's begin.
White light envelops the "candidate" in front of you. The heavy security arrangements in the interrogation room don't affect her at all.
Rise clasps her hands, sitting upright and composed.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Welcome to the interview, Miss Rise Blake.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I must thank you for your trust. You accepted my interview invitation so promptly that it saved me the cost of transportation subsidy for candidates.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: ...Chief, there probably isn't another interviewer in all of Eastside who can lighten the mood like you.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: I can tell, you probably don't usually handle MBCC's recruitment work.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You think the results aren't good?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Alright, then... I think we can skip the self-introduction part, don't you agree?

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: No objections there. We already have a basic understanding of each other.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: I've listed more information about myself on my resume. Feel free to use it as a base for your questions.
test
test
test
test
test
test
In her words and actions, Rise doesn't hide her confidence about her resume. And she indeed has the credentials to back it up.

The content on that thin sheet of paper, showcasing a graduate from a prestigious college with dual degrees in science and engineering, along with experience in top-tier companies, is so outstanding that it could raise doubts about its authenticity.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: With this resume, even if you don't look for a job, opportunities would come knocking at your door. It would be hard to find anyone with better qualifications than you, not just in the job market, but all of Eastside.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I've personally witnessed your performance during our previous collaboration together. I've never doubted your abilities.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So, I'm genuinely curious, why would you also encounter difficulties in job hunting?

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: ...It's simple. Because I'm not satisfied with those recruiting companies. Interviews are supposed to be a mutual selection process.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Before today, how many interviews have you gone to?

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Seventeen. I chose to accept the last offer. Ha, looking back now, that was the wrong choice.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: The number of interviews isn't indicative of anything. It just shows how many terrible companies there are in Eastside.
Rise's gaze shifts to the side. As she remembers, her brow furrows tighter, and a look of annoyance appears on her face.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Some change the job content on the spot. Some use tests to scam candidates. Some put hidden clauses in the contract to make it almost a slave contract...

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: If the interviews are already like this, I don't think employees will have safeguards after joining such companies.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Indeed. After joining, management might give you unrealistic demands that you can't refuse. Even during vacations, you can't get a breather, and you'll get unexpected tasks slapped onto you anytime, anywhere...

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: How familiar you are to all this, Chief. This could easily ruin my impression of the MBCC.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Sorry, it's just a bit of personal experience. Please don't take it to heart.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Alright... So in my view, the work environment in Eastside has become a cesspool of abuse, which deeply disappoints me. And what are the companies responsible for this dreadful state of affairs doing?

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Instead of addressing the problem, they tolerate and shield it. They can't even be bothered to deny responsibility, so they normalize it instead.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: They want to turn this twisted "normalcy" into "common sense" that everyone must accept, and then blame young people like me for being cynical and having unrealistic expectations. What a joke!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I sympathize with your situation, but what you mentioned might just be some extreme cases. After all, no company has flawless management, but there should be not-so-terrible places to work, too.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: You mean I've just been unlucky to not have encountered those "not-so-terrible" places?

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: I've tried so hard, but still haven't found a single job that meets my standards. This proves that the environment is the problem, not me.
Rise remains aloof, clearly disagreeing with your view.
Amidst the silent stalemate, you decide to quickly move on to the next "interview" question.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You're right. If it were me, I couldn't stand such an environment either.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Treating what is prevalent as what is right is just an excuse for self-deception because changing the status quo is too hard.
Your unquestioning agreement surprises Rise a bit. She looks at you with a probing gaze, seemingly trying to discern the truth in your words.
You decide to continue advancing the "interview."

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So in your mind, what does a satisfactory workplace look like?

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Have you ever heard of "Anniken"?
Rise's seemingly irrelevant response catches you off guard.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Anniken is the protagonist in Legend of the Star Realm, my favorite fantasy novel from my student days. In the story, he wields a lightsaber to save his homeland. Anniken was my very first idol.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: This surprises me a bit. I didn't expect you to like such... teenage literature.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Everyone goes through a phase of admiring heroes in novels.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: I've always admired people like Anniken and dreamed of a life like his—surrounded by like-minded companions, cutting through the darkness, fighting injustice, and bringing truth and righteousness to the world.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You're talking about the plot of a novel. How is this related to your desired workplace?

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: ...That's also what I'm trying to figure out.
Her voice suddenly turns cold. The gentle, dreamlike tone she had when describing the novel's plot vanishes.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Why does the environment I want only exist in novels and not in real life?

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: There's no place to shine and show your worth, nor is there a hero who will change the world. In reality, most people just go with the flow or contribute to our collective sins.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I respect and admire your persistence and ideals... but literature and real life are inherently different.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Moreover, changing the world has never been just one person's responsibility. You're putting too much pressure on yourself.
Rise gazes at you, as if making some silent judgment. For a moment, you feel as if you're the one being interviewed.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: I understand. But I've really had enough of this toxicity.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Even when I held myself to Anniken's standards, I simply could not accept what I saw and heard at the workplace. I couldn't help but take action.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: At first, I tried to fight back. But later I realized that exploitation and abuse are omnipresent in the job market. It's the same everywhere.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: But I also realized that what I can see is just the tip of the iceberg. My "naive" resistance cannot even touch the core of the matter.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: To truly change everything, I need a stronger power. Something that can overpower everything and set things right... just like Anniken's lightsaber.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: ...And then, I really acquired it.
She speaks as calmly as if discussing the weather.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: I became a Sinner.
The interrogation room falls into a brief silence. Rise sits upright in the interrogation chair with impeccable poise. You remain unperturbed after hearing her out.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: You don't seem surprised at all.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm just trying to understand what you mean... So, you're saying that you also have a "lightsaber" now?

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: ...I thought you'd be more concerned about me being a Sinner.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: I didn't expect you to tell me.

choices.text: I didn't expect you to tell me.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Maybe it's because there's no point in continuing to hide it from you.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: After all, you probably suspected it a long time ago. Right, Chief?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: When I went to Nirvana last time, my shackles sensed something unusual when you argued with the department head.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Moreover, you're the only survivor of the Nirvana attack and had serious conflicts with the victim before his death. Coupled with the Mania residue at the crime scene... all the clues point to you as a suspect.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Seems this interview is actually a follow-up investigation, then. Haha, so what do you really want to ask?

steps.speaker: Choice
options: Take out photos of the scene of the Nirvana attack

choices.text: Take out photos of the scene of the Nirvana attack

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: In addition to one death and one injury, the facilities at the meeting room were also severely damaged from the attack.
You lay out the photos side by side in front of Rise.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: All the damage marks were caused by the same sharp object. Tests found Mania residue in every cut, without exception.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Therefore, I speculate that the perpetrator is very likely a Sinner.
As you speak, you observe Rise's reaction. Her expression remains indifferent, even showing a hint of impatience.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: However, after further negotiations with Nirvana, the Public Security Bureau has decided to rule the case as an accident and drop further investigations.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: After all, if Nirvana as the "biggest victim" insists on not pursuing the matter, we "outsiders" have no reason to meddle.
Hearing your words, Rise pauses. Her gaze slowly shifts back to you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: And to be honest... though it's regrettable that someone died in the incident, I find it hard to feel sympathy for the deceased.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I interviewed many entry-level employees at Nirvana. I think those who were bullied by this manager would share my opinion.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: As for the attack...
You push the photos in front of you towards Rise.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Purely out of personal interest, I'm curious about the truth of the matter.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Rise, would you be willing to quench my curiosity?

In the interrogation room, you and Rise gaze at each other, trying to separate truth from lies and guess at each other's intentions. As you search in the dark to confirm an invisible trust, the brief, silent pause feels almost timeless.
Then, one of you speak up first.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: ...That evening, after work hours, in the meeting room...

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: When I was at my most furious... a lightsaber appeared in my hand. So I began to fight back for the first time.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Sir, it's less than half a month till the project deadline. When do you plan to fix its unrealistic direction and set up contingency plans?

steps.speaker: Department Supervisor
steps.content: Tsk... It's quite alright for you to have an attitude, being young and all, but don't get too sassy. Where are your manners?
In front of everyone, Rise stops the manager, who is idly monitoring the employees. She hands a finished report directly to him.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Time is tight. I've sent you four suggestions via email but got no response, so I had to come find you in person.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Whether it's market research or data analysis, the results completely contradict the project direction you insist on. This is a decision-making error on your part. As the department head, you should make adjustments as soon as possible.

steps.speaker: Department Supervisor
steps.content: Stop pointing fingers at me all the time. We're all in this together. Step up, take responsibility, and be a team player, Rise.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: I'm here to do my job, not to go out of my way to cover for you.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: If your stubbornness ultimately negates the entire department's efforts, then you are the sole culprit for this stupid mistake. No one else should bear that cost for you.

steps.speaker: Department Supervisor
steps.content: You...!
Mindful of their colleagues' gazes, the department manager takes a deep breath, continuing to force a smile.

steps.speaker: Department Supervisor
steps.content: You... have a point. Very well, Rise. The company needs employees like you who dare to speak up.

steps.speaker: Department Supervisor
steps.content: But it's not a good time to discuss this right now. Let's go over it in detail in the meeting room after work, alright?
<color=#fb9259>After work</color>
Rise quickly clasps her fist behind her back. She shuts her eyes and tries to calm the fury that surged to her throat.
Hidden from view in the palm of her hand, her clenched fingers have already disintegrated into strange particles and light.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: What in the world is going on? Lately, my body has been like this whenever I get emotional... As if the troubles at work aren't enough, now I have to deal with this weird problem as well.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Is it caused by too much stress? It's acting up again at this juncture... With a manager like him, it'll be hard to ask for sick leave.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Forget it. I'll just go to the squash court after tonight's meeting...
After several deep breaths, Rise's emotions stabilize, and her bodily anomalies gradually vanish.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: ...Better not worry about it for now.
After work, as everyone else gradually leaves, Rise follows the manager into a secluded meeting room.

steps.speaker: Department Supervisor
steps.content: First up, there's something you need to know...

steps.speaker: Department Supervisor
steps.content: You don't need to come in tomorrow.
As if worried she didn't understand, the man sits down in a chair, looks up at Rise, and loudly repeats himself.

steps.speaker: Department Supervisor
steps.content: After careful consideration by the department, you shall no longer work at Nirvana.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: What?

steps.speaker: Department Supervisor
steps.content: Someone anonymously reported that you have violent tendencies and caused panic among colleagues. Why are you so hostile at such a young age?

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: What is the basis for judging the truth of the report?

steps.speaker: Department Supervisor
steps.content: Ha, that I cannot say.

steps.speaker: Department Supervisor
steps.content: Nirvana strictly protects the anonymity of the informant, to guard against... malice from certain individuals.

steps.speaker: Department Supervisor
steps.content: It's best that you resign on your own, so we can all save face. Otherwise, the company will have to take stronger measures against you!
Rise laughs in anger at his shameless words.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Absurd! Do you know that this violates the DisCity Labor Ordinance?
The seated man tilts his head at Rise with a calm and smug grin.

steps.speaker: Department Supervisor
steps.content: And what can you do about it?

steps.speaker: Department Supervisor
steps.content: This meeting room will lose all of its surveillance footage due to a "technical glitch," leaving no trace of this conversation.

steps.speaker: Department Supervisor
steps.content: No one will follow up on it. And do you know why, Rise Blake?

steps.speaker: Department Supervisor
steps.content: Because it's the norm.
The manager's grotesque face distorts and magnifies before Rise's eyes, and his voice becomes increasingly grating.
Fury surges in Rise's chest, almost suffocating her. She vaguely senses a premonition of losing control. She clenches her fists by her sides, barely restraining her rage.
The man, still rambling on, doesn't notice Rise's anomalies.

steps.speaker: Department Supervisor
steps.content: Besides, you're in no position to be uppity.

steps.speaker: Department Supervisor
steps.content: You think a big company like Nirvana can't squash a little intern like you?
Anniken says:
For a moment, Rise seems to hear the sound of a string snapping inside her. But it might also be the crack of breaking free from shackles.
A bright and dazzling data lightsaber appears in her hand.
[Black screen, lightsaber slashing sound effect]
When Rise opens her eyes again, amidst the countless beams and particles erupting from her body, she sees everything that she had destroyed.
"I will use my lightsaber to cut through the filth and tear apart evil. The blade will guide me out of injustice and darkness."

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Later, I made the scene look like a mysterious attack, and pretended that I was also a victim.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Just as you had speculated, the culprit is a Sinner. That's the truth of the matter. Anything else you want to ask?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I have no more questions about the case. But I still have a few questions about you.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: About me?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Do you regret the consequences of your actions?

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: ...What consequences are you referring to? That I can't find a job, or the occurrence of that "accident"?
She sneers with disdain.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Regardless of which you're referring to, my answer is no, I do not regret it.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: When I wielded my lightsaber, all I felt was exhilaration! It's been so long since I've felt... so relieved.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: It's the best and most thorough way to eliminate workplace toxicity. I have nothing to regret.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If you truly have no regrets, why didn't you keep doing the same thing in similar situations later on?

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: That's like asking a criminal why they don't keep committing more crimes. This doesn't seem like something the MBCC Chief should say.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Why do you liken your embrace of violence to committing a crime?

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: I don't see the point in playing these word games. Can we move on to the next...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: What is it that truly makes you feel no regret—resorting to violence, or the fact that you finally stood up for yourself?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The exhilaration you felt from using the lightsaber was more about relief from stress than about violence. Your tension was about to break its limit, and violence became your final, desperate resort.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: However, the problems in the workplace weren't caused by you alone, nor should you bear the responsibility of correcting them all by yourself.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Rise, you put too much pressure on yourself.
The interrogation room falls silent. Rise's reflective glasses obscure her expression, making it hard for you to observe her emotions and reactions.
After a while, she looks up at you with exceptionally calm eyes.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: ...After that incident, I also realized the problem of stress.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Nirvana doesn't have the work environment I want, and I can't change it. If I continue to endure, it will only become the trigger for another pointless "incident."

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: That's why I chose to leave Nirvana and seek a new job.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You wanted to eliminate the stress caused by that toxic workplace from the root.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Yes, but...
She pauses, bearing the confused look of a traveler suddenly lost in a fog.
Then, she slowly continues, as if questioning you, or perhaps herself.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: But it's the same everywhere; Nirvana is just a snapshot of the overall toxicity of DisCity.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: What do you think I should do? Just find another company and continue to endure?

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: You see... even if the lightsaber can't eradicate the problem, it can at least eliminate some of the scum and have some short-term effects.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Is equality and respect maintained by violence really what you want? Rise, I don't think you'd condone such a self-righteous illusion.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Then tell me, what else can I do?

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: When one place fails me, I look for another, then another... It may seem like I'm on the search, but in reality, I'm just constantly fleeing!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Then stop looking.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Hmm...
You interrupt Rise, and she looks at you with a puzzled gaze.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm offering you another possibility.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If you can't find an existing work environment that's good enough, why not help create one?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If you think about it, the lightsaber is not just a weapon, but also a torch to find companions. A fair and comfortable workplace is a common wish for many.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So, Rise, would you consider working with others to create the workplace you want?

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: ...Chief, please be more direct.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Alright... I'll be more direct, then. If you want a place where you can work with peace of mind, the MBCC is a promising choice.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: There are still some problems now, but many of us here share your beliefs. I'm confident that you'll shine here.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But ultimately, this is an interview. I feel like I'm tooting my own horn.
You sigh helplessly. Rise clearly didn't expect you to still consider this an interview. After a brief pause, she chuckles softly.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Isn't this interview just an excuse for you to interrogate me?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: It's my duty as the Chief to interrogate, but this interview is my personal invitation to you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: This is a mutual selection, and my choice remains unchanged. Rise, now it's your turn to choose.
Rise glances at the electronic wristwatch on her wrist.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: ...It's about time to conclude this interview, then. To wrap things up, shouldn't we discuss the most important part about salary and benefits?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The position is quite special, so the salary isn't high... uh, or rather, almost nonexistent.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But it's not without advantages! We cover all living expenses, and it's very stable. You never have to worry about being laid off.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: ...Chief, you're really not suited to be an interviewer.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: However, I can accept what you offer.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You've made up your mind? Sure you don't want to compare it to some other offers?

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: If the price of a high salary is endless exploitation and abuse, then I'd rather not have it. Respect, equality, comfort... many things are much more important to me than money.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Given our previous experience working together, I think I have a good understanding of your abilities and character. After thinking about it... working for you is the most ideal choice for me right now.
You extend your hand again. This time, Rise grasps it tightly without hesitation.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Chief, I'm willing to trust you, for now. I hope you won't forget the promise you made to me today.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I will strive to extend this trust indefinitely.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I shall help you realize your vision and free you from those needless burdens. Someday, respect and equality will reign as the norm around here, and we'll bear witness to its final form together.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: ...That really sounds like something a hero like Anniken would do.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: I'm looking forward to it.
The red shackles pierce and connect your palms together. This is your "work contract" with Rise.
"The lightsaber will take me to my companions. I shall not walk alone down this path."
She is not the lonely one.
